Quick summary after parsing the CSV and running our throughput model:
- Baseline (moderate) recommendation: 10 x A100-slices (or equivalent Ampere/Oracle configs) configured as a single dedicated pool with autoscale headroom for 25% sustained bursts. This targets P95 <200ms for the 65% user-facing mix when we enable KV prefix caching and token-level batching of prompt templates.
- Conservative: 13 units for stronger headroom at 30–40% peak; Aggressive: 8 units plus more aggressive quantization to lower cost.

Cost delta note: expected hosted->dedicated token-unit cost reduction of 38% on the moderate profile (includes expected gains from batching/caching but not the one-time migration validation labor).

Proposed cutover cadence (public summary to send to customer):
1) Intake & sizing (1 business day after data validated)
2) Staging and stress validation (2 business days)
3) Canary (48h at 10% weight)
4) Progressive ramp day (4 hour morning window) with 30-minute stabilization checks and automated rollback guardrails

Attachments for customer: proposed_cutover_cadence_v2.pdf (runbook), commit-to-dedicated-psa.docx (procurement checklist)

— Priyom
